title: First job with the Columbia Band at Butcher Hill, age 16
summary: At sixteen Williams played his first job with the Columbia Band, naming its members including Tick Chambers, Ernest Kelly and Roy Palmer.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: How old were you when you started out?
When I started playing, when I played my first job, I was 16. I played with the Columbia Band up on Oak and Protection Levy at a place, a dance hall called Butcher Hill.
Oh, yeah. Johnny St. Sarah told me all the time.
Butcher Hill. Well, I played there with Columbia Band, Tick Chambers. I played in a fella's place. The drummer was with Tick Chambers by the name of Nene.

That's all I know, Nene. And I played there. We had, in the band at that time, we had Tick Chambers, Ernest Kelly. Ernest Johnson, a little fella they call Duck Ernest, I guess you heard of him. Mm-hmm. And Emmett, the guy who played guitar by the name of Emmett. I don't know, I can't think of his last name, Emmett. And a fella by the name of Roy Palmer, trombone. Oh, yeah, you played with Roy.
I know him in Chicago, yeah. Roy Palmer.
Roy Palmer, he was playing trombone. He was still up there.
I saw him last summer. Living. Yeah, he looks good. I don't know about that. Works in a steel mill, still works hard.
Now, what do you know about that? He does. Yes, indeed. That was my first band I played with. Now, my next band I played with was sitting in a guy's place was with Ori's band.
